Aims to assess people management, onboarding design, and practical trade-offs for early-stage teams.

## Key Concepts
- Mentorship and buddy systems
- Structured onboarding with measurable ramp
- Balancing velocity with ramp time
- Metrics that reflect integration, not just output

## Code Example

```javascript
const rampMetrics = {
  firstPRDays: 2,
  mergedPRs: 3,
  tasksCompleted: 4,
  velocityDelta: "+20%"
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt if one buddy becomes overloaded?
- What would you improve if onboarding takes longer than 2 weeks?

- Which artifact would you retire first if regulatory demands increase?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical onboarding, mentorship, and measurable ramp outcomes for junior engineers, essential for growing teams at Snowflake/Meta.

## Key Concepts
- Structured onboarding with milestones
- Mentorship and pair programming
- Ramp metrics (time-to-first-PR, task completion, defect rate)
- Risk management and escalation

## Code Example
```javascript
// Example onboarding checklist generator
function onboardingChecklist(roles, weeks = 8){
  const base = ['set up environment','read docs','pair with buddy','write a small feature'];
  return roles.flatMap(r => base.map(t => `${r} - ${t}`));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this plan for fully remote onboarding?
- What metrics would you use to decide when a ramp is complete?

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates your ability to design scalable leadership structures that maintain delivery velocity while developing technical depth and people management capabilities across distributed teams.

## Key Concepts
- Dual-track career ladders
- Technical leadership vs people management paths
- Cross-regional governance models
- Mentoring frameworks and cadences
- Shared OKRs for alignment
- Success metrics: velocity, turnover, time-to-promotion
- Phased rollout strategies

## Code Example

```javascript
{
  "pilot": "90 days",
  "cohorts": 2,
  "tracks": ["Technical Leader", "People Manager"],
  "regions": 4,
  "governance": "bi-weekly reviews",
  "okrs": {
    "technical": ["code quality", "architecture decisions"],
    "delivery": ["feature velocity", "team satisfaction"]
  },
  "metrics": ["velocity", "turnover", "time-to-promotion"]
}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates the ability to design practical, beginner-friendly incident response processes for distributed teams, assessing understanding of ownership structures, documentation requirements, training cadence, performance metrics, and validation approaches.

## Key Concepts
- Incident command rotation and on-call management
- Runbooks, escalation matrices, and postmortem frameworks
- Training drills and performance metrics (MTTR, burnout, participation)
- Experimental validation of readiness

## Code Example
```javascript
const incidentPlan = {
  command: "Team Rotation",
  artifacts: ["runbook", "escalation matrix", "postmortem template"],
  cadence: { drills: "bi-weekly", simulations: "monthly" },
  metrics: ["MTTR", "incident frequency", "burnout rate", "participation"],
  experiments: [
    "dashboard outage tabletop",
    "Sev1 partial availability",
    "cross-timezone handoff"
  ]
};
```
